title: "Nonlinear Least Squares Fitting (Finite Differences)"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Overview

This example demonstrates nonlinear least squares data fitting using finite-difference derivatives to fit a mixed log-normal and Gaussian distribution to density data, using the `aoclda` package.

```{r library}
library(aoclda)
```

## Model Functions

```{r functions}
n_res <- 64

lognormal_fn <- function(d, a, b, Al) {
    Al / (d * b * sqrt(2 * pi)) * exp(-((log(d) - a)^2) / (2 * b^2))
}

gaussian_fn <- function(d, mu, sigma, Ag) {
    Ag * exp(-0.5 * ((d - mu) / sigma)^2) / (sigma * sqrt(2 * pi))
}

res_fun <- function(x, data) {
    d <- data$d
    y <- data$y
    a <- x[1]
    b <- x[2]
    Al <- x[3]
    mu <- x[4]
    sigma <- x[5]
    Ag <- x[6]
    vapply(seq_len(n_res), function(i) {
        lognormal_fn(d[i], a, b, Al) + gaussian_fn(d[i], mu, sigma, Ag) - y[i]
    }, numeric(1))
}
```

## Fit

```{r fit}
n_coef <- 6
x0 <- c(1.63, 0.88, 1.0, 30, 1.52, 0.24)
w <- rep(1, n_res)
w[56:63] <- 5.0
w <- w / sum(w)
blx <- rep(0, n_coef)

ndf <- nlls$new(n_coef, n_res, weights = w, lower_bounds = blx, verbose = 2L)
x_fitted <- ndf$fit(x0,
    fun = res_fun, data = list(d = diameter, y = density),
    abs_gtol = 1e-7, gtol = 1e-7, fd_step = 5e-7
)

xexp <- c(2.02, 1.39, 0.693, 36.672, 6.96, 0.3368)

cat(sprintf("Solution found in %d iterations\n", ndf$n_iter))
cat(sprintf("Residual norm at solution: %.4e\n", ndf$metrics$obj))
cat("Solution:\n")
for (i in seq_along(ndf$coef)) {
  ok <- abs(ndf$coef[i] - xexp[i]) <= 1e-2
  cat(sprintf("x[%d] = %.3f  expected: (%.3f)  OK? %s\n", i, ndf$coef[i], xexp[i], ok))
}
```
